summary: Abdul Moyeen Khan, Andaleeve Rahman Partho, and Sa Ching Pru Jerry are expected to be sworn in as ministers, while Shamim Kaiser Lincoln is likely to be a state minister.

caption:
Four new faces are joining the cabinet today. Who are they?

Four more lawmakers are expected to join Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s cabinet today, with three taking oath as ministers and one as a state minister.

The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled to take place at Bangabhaban shortly after President-elect Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir takes his oath of office at 7:30pm today.

The prospective appointees include Abdul Moyeen Khan (Narsingdi-2), Andaleeve Rahman Partho (Bhola-1), and Sa Ching Pru Jerry (Bandarban), who are set to take oath as ministers.

Shamim Kaiser Lincoln is likely to be sworn in as a state minister.

The Cabinet Division has already contacted the prospective appointees and asked them to be present at Bangabhaban this evening.

Abdul Moyeen Khan is a member of the BNP standing committee, while Andaleeve Rahman Partho is the chairman of the Bangladesh Jatiya Party-BJP, a BNP ally.

headline: India withdraws notice on Tarique Rahman's visit preparations
summary: A statement indicating preparations at Rashtrapati Bhavan for a possible visit by the Bangladeshi prime minister was recalled shortly after being issued.
details: India's Press Information Bureau posted a press release this afternoon stating that the Change of Guard Ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan would be cancelled on Saturday, August 22, due to a rehearsal for the ceremonial welcome of the Bangladeshi prime minister.
The statement was quickly recalled shortly after it was issued at 2:25pm, with no official comments immediately available from officials in either Dhaka or Delhi.
A possible visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has been a central point of discussion between the foreign ministries of the two neighboring countries.
Officials had previously indicated that the visit could potentially take place in the third week of August.
However, Bangladesh's foreign ministry noted on August 16 that discussions regarding the visit have been complicated by the press appearance of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina on August 5.
caption:
India briefly issued and then withdrew a notice regarding preparations for a visit by the Bangladeshi prime minister.

India's Press Information Bureau posted a press release this afternoon stating that the Change of Guard Ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan would be cancelled on Saturday, August 22, due to a rehearsal for the ceremonial welcome of the Bangladeshi prime minister.

The statement was quickly recalled shortly after it was issued at 2:25pm, with no official comments immediately available from officials in either Dhaka or Delhi.

A possible visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has been a central point of discussion between the foreign ministries of the two neighboring countries.

Officials had previously indicated that the visit could potentially take place in the third week of August.

However, Bangladesh's foreign ministry noted on August 16 that discussions regarding the visit have been complicated by the press appearance of deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina on August 5.
